name: X-linked Juvenile Retinoschisis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Juvenile Retinoschisis

criteria.description: Bilateral foveal schisis with characteristic spoke-wheel pattern on fundus examination
Electroretinogram (ERG) showing reduced b-wave amplitude with relatively preserved a-wave
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the RS1 gene
Presence of peripheral retinal schisis on imaging
Positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical findings plus either supportive electrophysiology or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is considered definitive; ERG and fundus findings support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral foveal schisis with spoke-wheel pattern
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic retinal splitting seen on fundoscopy
searchTerms: central retinal splitting with spoke pattern
reduced b-wave in eye electrical test

common.notes: Usually presents in childhood or adolescence
searchTerms: worsening vision in center of eye

common.notes: May lead to peripheral vision defects

occasional.notes: Complication due to schisis cavity rupture
May develop secondary to poor vision
Visual flashes reported by some patients
Due to peripheral schisis or retinal detachment

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing splitting of retinal layers
Fundus photography demonstrating foveal schisis with spoke-wheel pattern
Fluorescein angiography typically normal or showing mild leakage
genetic: Pathogenic variants in RS1 gene on X chromosome
other: Electroretinogram with selective reduction of b-wave amplitude

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive peripheral vision loss with bone-spicule pigmentation
ERG shows generalized rod and cone dysfunction

redFlags: Sudden onset of floaters or flashes indicating retinal detachment
references: George ND, Yates JR, Moore AT. X-linked juvenile retinoschisis. Br J Ophthalmol. 1995;79(6):471-476.
Molday RS, Kellner U, Weber BH. X-linked juvenile retinoschisis: clinical diagnosis, genetic analysis, and molecular mechanisms. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2012;31(3):195-212.
